newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Profit-taking hits M&R after dispute news.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking hits M&R after dispute news.

text.p: News that Murray & Roberts had settled its Siemens dispute triggered active trade in the share on Thursday but failed to move it higher.

Dealers said that M&R shares had climbed substantially over the last week off lows fallen to last year and that profit-taking was being seen now that certainty over the dispute settlement was in the market.
M&R shares had shed 25 cents to 13.10 rand by 0850 GMT in a volume of 545,400 shares on an otherwise quiet morning. The share has climbed from 10.40 rand per share last Monday.
"It's been a star riser in the last week off its previous lows and now we're seeing profit-taking," one dealer said.
From the start of 1996 to its end, M&R lost nearly two-thirds of its value, falling to 9.80 rand a share on December 17, 1996 from 28.25 rand a share on January 23, 1996.

The local Business Day newspaper reported earlier that construction and engineering firm M&R had settled its dispute with German-based project manager Siemens over a 500 million rand Taiwanese train contract with M&R Union Carriage & Wagon.
M&R financial director Lionel Bird confirmed to the paper that settlement had been reached but declined to give further details until the group's related insurance claims had been settled.

The dispute, which relates to the carriages supplied to Siemens failing stress tests, has weighed on M&R's earnings since last year. The group announced in August that it had set aside a 160 million rand provision to deal.
It was unclear how much, if any, of the money would be recovered, the paper said.
